prompt: People’s shopping habits depend more on the age group they belong to than any other factors. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
The generation group is seen as a main factor influencing how people build their shopping habits. However, I believe that money is a primary indicator that creates those habits, because we need it the most in every purchase decision.

On the one hand, how old people affect their shopping habits. It influences the product types they choose to buy. For instance, the young generation nowadays often uses their pocket money to buy viral food or drink, such as a cheesecake or a matcha latte, while the old generation tends to buy warm and comforting food, like a camomile tea.

On the other hand, money acts as a main key in creating shopping habits, because every purchase needs money. As a result of how much money they have, they will have different habits. For example, the rich usually buy things because of their excellent quality, but the poor are more likely to see the price than the materials used. Therefore, though it is the same product as clothes or food, they will buy things differently. Moreover, those who do not have much money tend to save more once they earn and do not spend it easily. Meanwhile, the rich will buy everything they want as they can afford it.

In conclusion, the age group influence people's shopping habits, but the main factor is still the money that we have. How old we are will determine the product types we tend to buy, but it does nothing when there is no money as we need it in every purchase.
